Subject: Synergetic Health — post-demo recap & suggested trial playbook

Thanks again for your time today — appreciated the open discussion and the clear goals. Below is a concise recap and a suggested evaluation playbook so we can lock the kickoff and success criteria.

High-level scope (agreed):
- Replace existing NLU routing + entity extraction for appointment booking and insurance eligibility flows (two workloads).
- Surface deterministic audit logs and per-token telemetry for cost/latency analysis.

Proposed success criteria (initial):
- Latency: p50 <= 300ms, p95 <= 600ms for the interactive routing endpoint (95p added if you confirm).
- Throughput: support sustained 50 req/sec with burst to 100 req/sec for 60s windows without degradation of p95 SLA.
- Cost: average cost/token target <= $0.0008 during trial (end-to-end including batching).
- Quality: routing accuracy >= 92% (micro-F1 for intent), entity extraction F1 >= 0.85 on your labeled holdout.

Trial timeline (6 weeks recommended):
- Week 0 (pre-kickoff): exchange sample dataset + test harness (you provide); RDC will prep baseline config.
- Week 1 (kickoff + smoke): run smoke tests, baseline perf measurement.
- Week 3 (mid-run readout): quality and perf checkpoint, tuning pass.
- Week 6 (final readout): acceptance decision based on KPIs above.

Ownership (Redwood):
- Monica Patel — primary account lead / kickoff coordinator
- Ben Carter — performance engineering / benchmark owner
- Jonas Weber — infra/SRE / test capacity & logs

Next steps I propose (actionable):
1) Confirm you agree with the success criteria above (esp. p95 threshold).
2) Share sample dataset + test harness by EOD Wednesday (5/5).
3) Kickoff meeting: propose Monday 5/9 10am PT — confirm availability.

Attachments: synergetic_poc_playbook_v1.xlsx (playbook draft), redwood_perf-targets-20270503.pdf (perf target notes)

Thanks — I’ll wait for confirmation on the p95 item and the dataset cadence.

—

Thanks Monica — quick confirmation from our side and a couple of constraints to call out.

We agree in principle with the scope. A few notes:
- Procurement/legal will need an SOW and the mutual action plan (MAP) in advance of kickoff; we’ll aim to get comments back within 3 business days.
- Data residency: all test traffic must remain in our US region (no cross-region replication for logs during the trial).
- Performance tolerance: we agree to the p50 target but need p95 <= 600ms (we flagged this during the demo). If Redwood can guarantee p95 <=600ms for interactive routing under the stated throughput, we’re good.

We will deliver the anonymized sample dataset + the test harness (JMeter script + expected labels) by EOD Wed 5/5.

For kickoff, Monday 5/9 10am PT works for Evan and Priya. Procurement will be looped and may push a separate short call if legal redlines appear.

On attachments: please include the mutual-action-plan.docx you mentioned so our procurement can start review concurrently.

Couple of pragmatic notes from the performance engineering side — putting these here so the perf baseline is actionable.

Baseline measurement plan (Ben / Redwood):
- Workload slices: 3 (routing-heavy; entity-heavy; mixed).
- Samples: 5k labeled requests per slice (use your labeled holdout).
- Measurement: run 3 independent runs for statistical stability; report p50/p95, token cost, GPU utlization, and tail latencies.

Configuration & tuning suggestions:
- Use dynamic batching with max batch size 64 and latency cap of 250ms for routing endpoint; this balances cost and p95.
- Recommend int8 quantized variant for entity extraction to reduce token cost; we will run quality regression tests to validate F1 drop < 1.5 pts.
- Expect cost/token in the trial to be ~ $0.00065–$0.0009 depending on batching — will provide a measured rollup.

Deliverables & timing:
- Perf baseline artifact (spreadsheet + perf plots) by 2027-05-12 (Ben).
- Tuning recommendations + size-of-change appendix by 2027-05-14 (Ben).

If Synergetic can provide a 5k sample per slice by Wed EOD, we’ll start runs Thu and have preliminary numbers for the kickoff.

—
Ben Carter
